perspective_statement.label: Epistemic Perspective
perspective_statement.focus: treat the search as a process of learning where the inferential bottleneck really sits
perspective_statement.warning: do not mistake richer organization or higher route articulation for solved mathematics
perspective_statement.interpretation: read the current state conservatively but allow genuine programme-level learning to count as progress

original_hardness.summary: p-vs-np is hard in this KB because global targets are framed across multiple incompatible proof regimes, barrier theorems restrict generic techniques, and explicit dependencies are sparse, forcing hypothesis-driven bridge construction.

hardness_elements.title: Cross-regime proof movement remains difficult.
hardness_elements.detail: The current route still requires movement from a weak-model lower bound regime to a stronger separation consequence through a bridge object rather than by direct deduction.

hardness_elements.title: Barrier pressure is now more localized than before.
hardness_elements.detail: The bridge portfolio names the carrier as `MCSP witness family`, while the selected proof sketch currently operationalizes the route through `Gap-MCSP promise problem`. This is an unresolved representation shift inside the current macro-proof state, not a proved equivalence.

current_proof_state_interpretation.headline: The current proof state should be read as a conditional research programme rather than as a near-complete proof.
current_proof_state_interpretation.detail: The decisive bottleneck is the leading magnification bridge. The final reduction from the nonuniform target to the main conjecture is already available, so the strategic question is whether the bridge object can be fixed and the source-realization, transport, route, and payoff lemmas can be discharged.
current_proof_state_interpretation.not_yet: It is not yet a solved proof of `P != NP` because the leading bridge still lacks discharged source-realization, transport, route, and payoff lemmas.

shifts_of_understanding.label: perspective-shift
shifts_of_understanding.title: The main problem is no longer being approached as a direct P versus NP proof.
shifts_of_understanding.before: The ambient question is the direct conjecture `P != NP`.
shifts_of_understanding.after: The current programme first targets `NP not in P/poly` and only then returns to `P != NP` through the grounding implication.
shifts_of_understanding.significance: This is a genuine reframing of the search unit, because it replaces a monolithic open problem with a theorem-pair-specific route target.

shifts_of_understanding.label: sharpening
shifts_of_understanding.title: The bridge has become object-level rather than merely topical.
shifts_of_understanding.before: The hidden transport in the route could be discussed only as a generic bridge or magnification idea.
shifts_of_understanding.after: The current route is organized around the typed carrier `MCSP witness family` and a named preserved invariant.
shifts_of_understanding.significance: This sharpens the inferential burden from 'find a connection' to 'realize, transport, and cash out a specific bridge object'.

shifts_of_understanding.after: The bridge portfolio names the carrier as `MCSP witness family`, while the selected proof sketch currently operationalizes the route through `Gap-MCSP promise problem`. This is an unresolved representation shift inside the current macro-proof state, not a proved equivalence.
shifts_of_understanding.significance: This is progress in inspectability but not yet in closure; the framework now knows exactly where the representation defect sits.

shifts_of_understanding.label: sharpening
shifts_of_understanding.title: The proof frontier is now theorem-sized and file-backed.
shifts_of_understanding.before: Open work existed only as a diffuse set of bridge or strategy obligations.
shifts_of_understanding.after: The process now exposes a persistent queue with 56 pending theorem-shaped proof targets and explicit route lemmas.
shifts_of_understanding.significance: This changes the discovery process from free exploration into an auditable sequence of prove-or-disprove tasks.

shifts_of_understanding.label: persistence
shifts_of_understanding.title: The central hardness still persists as missing proof-carrying evidence.
shifts_of_understanding.before: The original problem was hard because routes spanned incompatible regimes and lacked explicit transfer mechanisms.
shifts_of_understanding.after: The current state still lacks terminal proof resolution (`proved_count=0`) and still shows low external pressure (`evidence_count=0`).
shifts_of_understanding.significance: The process has localized the bottleneck, but it has not yet dissolved it.

meta_judgment.headline: The discovery process has genuinely improved understanding of where the problem is hard, but it has not yet produced evidence that the main conjecture is close to resolution.
meta_judgment.detail: What changed is the granularity of the problem: the search now isolates a sharper target, a typed carrier, a representation defect, and a queue of inspectable obligations. What persists is the absence of terminal proof evidence, adversarial stress, and representation closure.

references.title: Definition of P
references.excerpt: P is the class of languages decidable by deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines.

references.title: Definition of NP
references.excerpt: NP is the class of languages whose yes instances admit polynomial-size certificates verifiable in polynomial time.

references.title: Definition of NP-completeness
references.excerpt: A language is NP-complete if it lies in NP and every language in NP polynomial-time many-one reduces to it.

references.title: Definition of P/poly
references.excerpt: P/poly is the class of languages decided by polynomial-size Boolean circuit families, equivalently polynomial-time computation with polynomial-length advice.

references.title: Nonuniform separation target
references.excerpt: If NP is not contained in P/poly, then P != NP.

references.title: Leading-route source
references.excerpt: A hardness magnification theorem has the form:"A barely-nontrivial lower bound for an explicit problem Q in a weak model implies a major lower bound/separation in a strong model."Typically, Q is a meta-problem (e.g. a Gap-MCSP variant) and"major"means consequences such as NP not in P/poly.

references.title: Leading-route target
references.excerpt: In refined regimes, lower bounds for Gap-MCSP slightly beyond known frontiers (e.g. N^ 1+varepsilon -type circuit lower bounds for suitable promise gaps and input length N=2^n ) imply major consequences such as NP not in P/poly.

references.title: bridge.002
references.excerpt: There exist explicit"meta"problems (including MCSP variants) such that proving certain barely-superlinear lower bounds against restricted models (e.g. formulas) would imply major lower bounds for NP in much stronger models (including superpolynomial formula/circuit lower bounds, and in some parameter regimes consequences as strong as NP not in P/poly ).

references.title: bridge.016
references.excerpt: There exist general-purpose magnification theorems (not problem-specific) showing that certain mild lower bounds for distinguishers/sparse-code objects can be amplified into stronger circuit/formula lower bounds, achieving magnification thresholds below previously known lower bounds in some settings.
